correctness.rationale: Every order-three ternary de Bruijn unfolding has 27 unique trigrams; any full attractor must mark at least 9 positions, and the only size-9 possibility is indices 2,5,...,26. All size-10 sets hitting these 27 trigrams satisfy exactly the initial/gap/final inequalities, giving precisely 275 choices. Full-factor coverage is equivalent to hitting those trigrams plus each of 3 letters and 9 digrams. The included compiled checker enumerates all 373248 rotation classes by directed Euler tours (fixed unique 000 edge), all 27 cuts each, and all needed candidates. The output 8274096 size-9 and 1803600 size-10 verifies completeness and sharpness. The finite theorem is not generalized by extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The full-text Whittington paper establishes a favorable prime-order Lyndon cycle and one unfavorable ternary cut, but explicitly asks whether every cycle admits a favorable cut; this exact census shows 1632 counterexample cycles, with an exact 9/10 distribution for all cuts. The full-text Mantaci paper gives general bounds and an example, not the all-cycle finite classification. published-finding corpus and relevant prior-result comparisons found no covering claim. Priority outside accessible sources remains unproved.
residual_risks: An unpublished or poorly indexed exhaustive ternary order-three attractor census may exist; title/abstract searches cannot exclude it. The certificate is an exhaustive finite computation and does not address other alphabet sizes or orders.

value.rationale: This is an exhaustive classification of an objectively defined natural finite family directly motivated by a published de Bruijn string-attractor question. Its 1632 counterexample cycles settle negatively the universal question whether every ternary order-three cycle has some nine-optimal cut, while the exact 9/10 cut counts and ten-witness search give a complete sharp boundary. The importance is structural and not merely that code runs.
